name: max-pages
description:
Proves the max_pages parameter actually drives the pager() bound rather than being decorative. The scenario passes max_pages=2 and serves three pages with three DIFFERENT nextPageTokens, so the no-progress check cannot fire and every page carries a token, meaning the only thing that can end this walk is the ceiling -- which is what makes the stop attributable to the parameter.

Hitting the ceiling now RAISES via pager() rather than logging a friendly truncation line: an incomplete import is reported as an error instead of looking complete. The two pages reported before the raise are still imported, because the script streams per page. log_contains pins the pager error naming the loop label.

when_exhausted is `empty` ONLY as a terminator for a regression: the harness's empty response is a bare array, which this script rejects as the wrong shape, so a walk that stopped reading the parameter would take the third page and then stop on that one request later -- failing on request_count and the missing log line rather than running to the 100,000-page CONFIG backstop and timing out.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy: the id is the bare Stairwell asset number with no tenant scope.
